issue_prefix.description: Issue identifier prefix, e.g. "ENG" for ENG-42. Letters, digits, underscore or hyphen, 1-16 characters; "" clears it and identifiers fall back to the first three letters of the crew slug.

FinalAuthUserPreferenceValue.description: Arbitrary JSON value stored for the authenticated user and preference key.

FinalAuthWebhookPayload.description: Arbitrary JSON payload forwarded to the webhook pipeline.

color.description: Gradient-palette id; "" clears it, omit to keep the stored value.

icon.description: Crew-icon name; "" clears it, omit to keep the stored value.

info.description: Generated from internal/api/router_*.go route registrations (cmd/gen-openapi). Paths, methods, parameters, status branches, and audited read response schemas are source-derived; remaining request/response bodies use a generic fallback — see cmd/gen-openapi/main.go.
info.title: Crewship API

inputs.description: Values may reference the triggering entry with {{ event.mission_id }}, {{ event.agent_id }}, {{ event.crew_id }}, {{ event.run_id }} and {{ event.payload.<key> }}.

debounce_seconds.description: How long the enqueued run stays open for further matching events to coalesce into.

event_type.description: A journal entry type, e.g. mission.status_change. Exactly one per rule. Checked at save time against the server's closed registry of every entry type actually declared or emitted; a value outside that registry is refused with 400, naming real alternatives.

payload_equals.description: Every pair must equal the corresponding journal payload field. Empty matches every entry of the event type. For an event type covered by the server's curated payload-key map, a key its emitter never writes is REJECTED at save time (400) naming the real keys — mission.status_change carries action, details, and (on a status transition) from and to. For an event type NOT covered by that map, a key the emitter never writes is accepted and matches nothing; POST /automations/preview names the offending clause either way.

max_per_hour.description: Cap on runs this rule may cause per rolling hour. Over the cap, matches are dropped and one automation.throttled journal entry is written for the window.

when.description: Reserved for a future expression predicate. Accepted and ignored today.

blocking.description: A blocking hook runs synchronously and may veto the intercepted action.

event.description: One of the declared lifecycle events; an unknown value is rejected and the error lists the valid ones.

last_produced_at.description: Newest produced_at across the page's visible panels. NOT updated_at, which §10 defines as the SPEC's modification time — a page edited an hour ago whose data last arrived a week ago must not read as "updated today".

panel_count.description: Every panel on the page, sealed ones included — the grid draws a placeholder for those, so a count that skipped them would disagree with what the page renders.

panels.description: The parsed spec (§11b.2). The CLI parses the YAML document and sends this; the server validates it and checks that every declared owner crew and producer routine or agent resolves (§10b.1).

icon.description: Optional. The panel's glyph, from a CLOSED set (internal/pages/icons.go) — a name the client has no glyph for would render a blank header, which is a quieter failure than an unknown schema. Absent means the icon the panel's schema implies. There is no per-icon colour: colour on a panel means state.

id.description: The author-chosen panel id. It is the address a producer pushes to, so it is stable across edits.

issue.description: `crew/<slug>` — the crew an SLA lapse or a producer failure opens an issue on, once per lapse (§4 rule 4).

owner.description: `crew/<slug>`. This is the ACL, not a label: a viewer outside the crew never receives the panel (§7.1 rule 2).

producer.description: `<kind>/<ref>`, kind ∈ {routine, script, agent, webhook}. Only the declared producer may write the panel's payload (§7.1 rule 4).

refresh.description: Optional, and CLOSED. The event that RUNS this panel's producer — a trigger, not a hint: a page holds no query, so nothing polls and a refresh that does not run the producer refreshes nothing. `on:wake` fires when a wake gate ANYWHERE on this page fires; `on:panels-changed` fires when the page's panel list changes (a rename is not a panel change). Each compiles to an `automations` row with `action_kind: routine`, so the producer run is debounced, coalesced, rate-capped and priced against the chain-depth budget like any other automation. Refused at save time: a value outside the set; a producer that is not `routine/<slug>` (the server cannot run a script, call a webhook producer, or dispatch an agent — an agent is woken by a gate's `writes:`); `on:wake` on a page that declares no gate; and `on:wake` on a panel that declares its own gate, which is a loop.

schema.description: The set is CLOSED — a new panel kind is a server release. Five are always producible; embed.v1 is producible only where the operator has vetted an allow-list (CREWSHIP_PAGES_EMBED_SOURCES), so on an instance with none a page spec cannot declare one.

sla_seconds.description: Required and greater than zero: a panel without an SLA does not validate, and there is no default that means "never mind" (§4 rule 1).

span.description: 1–12 columns of the grid. Absent means 12.

tab.description: Optional. The tab this panel renders under (internal/pages/tabs.go). Bar order is FIRST APPEARANCE in the panel list, and a panel with no tab lands on the first tab; a page where no panel declares one has no bar. Each tab carries the worst state of its own panels, and the page's freshness summary is computed over ALL tabs — a hidden tab must never be a place a panel can go stale quietly (§4).

wake.description: Thresholds that turn this panel into a sensor (§5). Each compiles to an `automations` row owned by the page spec. Max 4 per panel.

agent.description: `crew/<slug>` — the crew woken when the gate fires. A crew and never a single agent.

for.description: Go duration. The condition must hold this long, continuously, before the gate fires, so one bad scrape wakes nobody. Max 24h.

when.description: The threshold, in one of two forms: `any(state == "critical")` / `all(state == "ok")` over a status.v1 panel, or `value > 90` over a metric.v1 panel. Not an expression language; a predicate the panel's schema cannot satisfy is refused at save time rather than never matching (§5).

writes.description: The panel the woken agent is expected to write. Must exist on this page. A declaration, not a grant: the agent still needs produce authority on it.

owner.description: `user/<id>` or `crew/<slug>` — exactly one of the two (§7.1 rule 1).

panels.description: Every panel on the page, in spec order. A panel owned by a crew the caller does not belong to arrives as the sealed placeholder — decided server-side, before serialisation, never hidden client-side (§7.1 rule 5, §11b.14).

data.description: The last payload, exactly as the producer sent it. Absent when nothing has ever been pushed.

icon.description: Optional. The panel's glyph, from a CLOSED set (internal/pages/icons.go) — a name the client has no glyph for would render a blank header, which is a quieter failure than an unknown schema. Absent means the icon the panel's schema implies. There is no per-icon colour: colour on a panel means state.

producer.description: `<kind>/<ref>`, kind ∈ {routine, script, agent, webhook}. Only the declared producer may write the panel's payload (§7.1 rule 4).
The panel's declared producer, `<kind>/<ref>`. Server-attached (§4 rule 5): a producer never claims it.

run_id.description: The pipeline run that produced the payload. A script or webhook producer has no run, and carries the push's own server-side reference (`push:<panel>:<seq>`) instead.

reason.description: Why a failed panel failed. Internal vocabulary — never rendered on a public page (§7.3.2b).

Refused at save time: a value outside the set; a producer that is not `routine/<slug>` (the server cannot run a script, call a webhook producer, or dispatch an agent — an agent is woken by a gate's `writes:`); `on:wake` on a page that declares no gate; and `on:wake` on a panel that declares its own gate, which is a loop.
